Definition: Number of operating years analyzed after the purchase year (years 0..T)
Effect on calculation: Sets T; replacements are bought at s + n·L < T and residual value is taken at T
Should come from: Contract term or main asset life; user
Source: DTN/Progressive Farmer (5-yr collar warranty); Reuter, Oklahoma State (36-month commitment); NRCS E614A (10-yr enhancement life)
Data year: Prices and terms as reported Mar 2025 and Jan 2025; program sheet Sept 2024
Evidence type and limits: Vendor warranty and contract term; program life assumption
Suggested value or range: Set by the user [D], usually the contract term or the main asset's life. Anchors: 5-yr collar warranty [C]; 36-month commitment [C]; 10-yr monitoring life [B]. Synthetic examples use 7 and 10 years [E]. The five-year test (next row) re-runs the analysis with the payback target in place of T

Definition: The number of years N within which the user wants the technology to pay for itself. Shown in step 2 next to the horizon
Effect on calculation: Sets N for the N-year test (B9): the whole analysis re-run with horizon N in place of T, every other input unchanged; straight-line residuals, including the lost residual of avoided fence, are valued at year N, and pctOfCost and amount residuals are used as entered. "Pays for itself within N years" means the N-year test's cash NPV ≥ 0 (operator share, before tax, cash lines only, at the analysis's real rate). If N > T, the test runs past the main horizon with every price unchanged and the page says "assumes the same prices continue to year N". The "What would make it pay" panel solves each driver that the module's `PAYBACK_DRIVERS(a)` returns by bisection, other inputs fixed, for the value at which the N-year cash NPV is 0 and the value at which the full-horizon cash NPV is 0 (the prototype's targetTest reproduces the N-year test; Appendix A). The headline stays the full-horizon cash NPV
Source: none
Evidence type and limits: No published source; the 5-year default is the owner's decision of 15 Oct 2026 (B9). It is a setting, not an estimate: values the "What would make it pay" panel reports are calculated from the other inputs, not sourced. The N-year result is not called payback because it counts residual value (judgment)
Suggested value or range: Default 5 years (owner decision, 15 Oct 2026), editable [D]. Stored in a v2 link only when it differs from 5; v1 links get 5. Synthetic examples: 5 years [E]

Definition: Minimum real return the money must earn: about the loan rate plus a risk premium, minus expected inflation. All prices are in today's dollars
Effect on calculation: Discounts every year's net cash
Should come from: User (loan rate, own required return, expected inflation)
Source: U. Wyoming B-1302 Net Present Value ("The minimum discount rate that should be used is the interest rate on any loan used to make the investment"); UF/IFAS FE1060; az2117 (3.9%)
Applicability: Any; az2117 rate is for Arizona ranch assets
Evidence type and limits: Extension method guidance. The sources give the method, not a rate for a given ranch
Suggested value or range: Set by the user for their own operation [D]. Each synthetic example loads with a visible, editable example rate of 7% real [E], so results appear at once; the page labels it "Example assumption (real rate), not a recommendation. Review it for your operation." When the user starts their own analysis, the rate keeps its value, the page shows a "Review this rate" prompt with the help text "real rate ≈ your loan rate + a risk premium − expected inflation", and the verdict carries "Discount rate not yet reviewed" until the user confirms or edits it; results are never blocked (owner decision, 15 Oct 2026). No rate is recommended: the owner has not selected one, and 7% is only the examples' value. For comparison only: az2117 used 3.9% and B-1302's worked example 10% [B]
